_readme: KNOWN LOCATIONS FOR CHAINS WHOSE FULL ROSTER WE DO NOT HAVE.
The archive already holds two shapes of partial knowledge: a census (a complete roster,
re-read daily, which can produce openings and closures) and a count without a roster
(Haidilao's parent saying '13 US restaurants' and naming none). This file is the third
shape — individual locations we know about for a chain whose complete list we cannot get.
These NEVER enter stores, observations or events. That is the whole point. If a partial
roster went into the census, then the day a complete source is finally read, every store in
it beyond this list would be recorded as an OPENING that never happened — fabricated growth,
which is worse than an empty row. Sightings are drawn on the map as open squares, labelled
as known-but-not-counted, and excluded from every total.
A sighting graduates by being deleted: when a chain's real locator is found, its adapter
supersedes this file and these entries should go.

locations.name: Tustin (楊銘宇─中國黃燜雞飯)
status_conflict: TWO SOURCES DISAGREE ABOUT THIS ADDRESS, and the disagreement is more valuable than
either claim. Yang's own store page presents it as trading: current hours, a phone
number, no closure notice. Yelp, updated September 2026 with 354 reviews, marks the same
address CLOSED — as it also does for the Culver City and Cupertino stores.
This was Yang's FIRST US restaurant, opened Tustin, September 2017. If Yelp is right,
the chain's own locator is carrying a store that shut — which would make that locator
nearly worthless for this project's actual purpose. A census detects closures by a store
DISAPPEARING from the list; a list that never removes anything can never produce one, and
would report a permanently growing chain no matter what happened on the ground.
Unresolved here, deliberately. Recorded so that whoever collects Yang's checks this first.
